meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Imagine all the people living life in peace'?
meta.ogDescription: A genuine lyric from John Lennon’s “Imagine” (1971) — with Yoko Ono added as co-writer in 2017. Still in copyright.

answer.label: Sung by
answer.authorDates: 1940–1980 · English musician, member of the Beatles (Yoko Ono credited co-writer since 2017)
answer.sourceLine: This is a genuine lyric from “Imagine,” the title track of John Lennon’s 1971 album, released as a single the same year. The wording — “Imagine all the people / Living life in peace” — matches the song exactly, and the official John Lennon site ↗ renders it that way. In 2017 Yoko Ono was formally added as a co-writer, honoring Lennon’s own 1980 statement that much of the lyric and concept came from her.

source.heading: The source
source.excerpt: Imagine all the people / Living life in peace… / You may say I’m a dreamer / But I’m not the only one
trail: The line is the second verse of “Imagine,” the 1971 title track of Lennon’s album, confirmed by Wikipedia’s article on the song ↗.
The official John Lennon website ↗ quotes the line exactly as “Imagine all the people living life in peace.”
In 2017 the National Music Publishers Association added Yoko Ono as co-writer, per NPR ↗, honoring Lennon’s own 1980 remark that the lyric and concept largely came from her.
source.excerptNote: The second verse of “Imagine.” Some printed lyric sheets render the line as “Livin’ life in peace”; the official John Lennon site uses “Living life in peace.”
source.rightsHolder: Estate of John Lennon and Yoko Ono (Lenono Music); administered by the song’s music publisher
source.rightsNote: “Imagine” was written and first published in 1971, far later than 1931, so it is firmly in copyright in the United States. Adding Yoko Ono as a co-writer in 2017 further extended the copyright term, since protection now runs from the death of the last surviving author.

author.name: John Lennon
author.heading: About John Lennon
author.metaLine: 1940–1980 · English singer-songwriter, co-founder of the Beatles, peace activist
author.bio: John Lennon was a founding member of the Beatles and, after the band split, a solo artist and activist. His 1971 song “Imagine” became one of the most recognized peace anthems of the 20th century. He said in 1980 that much of its lyric and concept came from his wife, Yoko Ono, who was formally credited as co-writer in 2017.

misattribution.heading: The real story: a genuine lyric with a hidden co-author
misattribution.intro: The line is correctly credited to John Lennon — it’s an authentic lyric from “Imagine” (1971), not a fabricated or misattributed quote. The twist is about who else wrote it.

items.why: Lennon admitted in a 1980 BBC interview that “a lot of the lyric and the concept came from Yoko” but that he had “omitted to mention her contribution.” She received a formal co-writing credit only in 2017, per Variety ↗.

misattribution.truthLine: The quote is real and genuinely Lennon’s — but the song is now officially credited to Lennon & Ono, per the 2017 NMPA decision ↗.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: “Imagine” asks listeners to picture a world without the divisions — nations, religion, possessions — that set people against one another. The line “Imagine all the people living life in peace” is the song’s emotional core, an invitation rather than a demand.
It became a global peace anthem, sung at vigils, Olympic ceremonies, and New Year’s celebrations, and remains one of the most-covered songs of the modern era.
